nodes.name: In-Flight Service (IFS) – Digital Sales & Operations Platform

overview.overview: A digital, offline-first in-flight sales and operations platform that enables cabin crew to record sales and inventory on mobile devices while providing centralized visibility for airline operations and management teams.

detailedDescription.detailedDescription: In-Flight Service (IFS) is a web and mobile platform designed to digitize in-flight sales and operational workflows. It enables cabin crew to manage sales and inventory offline during flights, while administrators and management gain centralized visibility through real-time dashboards and reports once data is synchronized.

challengeContent.challengeContent: Airlines relied heavily on manual, paper-based methods for recording in-flight sales and inventory, leading to errors, stock mismatches, and payment discrepancies—especially during multi-leg journeys with limited connectivity.

challengekeyPoints: Unreliable or unavailable internet connectivity during flights
Manual paper-based sales and inventory tracking
Payment failures during in-flight card transactions
Difficulty tracking unsold inventory accurately
Different access needs for crew, admins, and management

solutionContent.solutionContent: IFS introduces an offline-first digital platform that enables accurate sales and inventory tracking during flights, with secure synchronization and centralized monitoring for operational teams.

solutionKeyPoints: Offline-capable mobile application for cabin crew
Automated stock updates and payment failure handling
Support for multiple flight legs in a single journey
Role-based access for crew, administrators, and management
coreCapability: Offline In-Flight Sales Recording -- Allows cabin crew to record sales and inventory changes without internet connectivity and sync data securely after flights.
Automated Inventory Management -- Tracks sold and unsold inventory accurately with automated stock reconciliation.
Payment Exception Handling -- Manages card payment failures and ensures proper reconciliation of successful and failed transactions.
Centralized Reporting Dashboard -- Provides office and management teams with clear visibility into sales, stock levels, and operational performance.
businessImpact: 100% -- Elimination of manual, paper-based in-flight sales records
Accurate -- Reliable sales, payment, and inventory data across all flight legs
Efficient -- Faster workflows for cabin crew and administrative teams
Transparent -- Centralized, data-driven reporting for management decisions
keyOutcomes: Paperless In-Flight Operations -- Replaced manual documentation with a fully digital sales and inventory system.
Reduced Discrepancies -- Minimized payment mismatches and inventory losses through automated tracking.
Improved Operational Efficiency -- Streamlined workflows for cabin crew, admins, and management teams.
Data-Driven Decision Making -- Enabled management to access accurate reports for better operational control and planning.

nodes.name: DCS — Guest Bridge Application-Passenger Contact & Booking Data Integration

projectStory.projectStory:
Departure Control Systems (DCS) play a critical role in managing flight operations and passenger movement. However, the core DCS does not store or expose passenger contact details, such as mobile numbers, directly from booking data. This limitation created communication gaps and operational challenges, especially when teams needed to contact passengers close to departure time.
The Guest Bridge Application was introduced as a supporting layer alongside the existing DCS. It retrieves passenger contact and booking information from booking systems using PNR data and makes it available within operational workflows—without modifying core DCS functionality or increasing manual effort.

Passenger details are required close to departure time
Repeated booking system queries could impact system performance
strategyKeyPoints: Integration layer operating alongside the existing DCS
Automated data retrieval through scheduled background jobs
Filtering and de-duplication logic to minimize unnecessary booking system calls
Controlled and secure APIs to expose passenger contact details to authorized workflows
Seamless integration without changes to core DCS logic
impactResult: Passenger mobile numbers available when required for operations
Reduced manual effort and communication delays
Avoided duplicate and unnecessary booking system calls
Enabled smooth and timely passenger communication workflows
Improved data accuracy and consistency within DCS operations

collaboration.collaboration: The application was developed in close collaboration with operations teams and system owners to ensure seamless integration with existing DCS workflows. Data flow, synchronization timing, and usage patterns were carefully aligned with real operational processes, while a strong focus on reliability ensured minimal impact on overall system performance.

conclusion.conclusion: The DCS Guest Bridge Application successfully addressed a critical data gap without disrupting existing systems. By introducing a dedicated middleware layer, the solution enabled timely access to passenger contact information, improved operational communication, and ensured data consistency—demonstrating a scalable and non-intrusive approach to system integration in airline operations.
